name: Quick Mode for Ad-Hoc Tasks
description: Add 'fade quick' command for small tasks that don't warrant a full PRD. Maintains FADE guarantees (atomic commits, progress tracking) without PRD ceremony. Inspired by GSD's /gsd:quick which bypasses optional planning steps while maintaining quality guarantees.

userStories.title: Basic quick command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run 'fade quick "fix typo in README"' to do small tasks without creating a PRD
acceptanceCriteria: fade quick "task description" command exists
Launches Claude Code with task description as prompt
Does not require PRD file to exist
Works in both FADE-initialized and non-FADE projects
Documented in fade help

userStories.title: Quick mode context injection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want quick mode to still use FADE.md context so Claude understands my project
acceptanceCriteria: If FADE.md exists, it's included in context
If standards/ folder exists, relevant standards are included
Context is minimal - just FADE.md and task, no PRD protocol
Quick mode prompt instructs single-task completion, not story workflow

userStories.title: Atomic commit on completion
userStories.description: As a developer, I want quick mode to create an atomic commit when done so my git history stays clean
acceptanceCriteria: Quick mode prompt instructs Claude to commit changes when done
Commit message derived from task description
Uses conventional commit format (fix:, docs:, chore:, etc.)
Only commits if changes were made

userStories.title: Quick task logging
userStories.description: As a developer, I want quick tasks logged to progress.md so I have a record of ad-hoc work
acceptanceCriteria: Quick mode prompt instructs appending to progress.md
Log format: '## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM - QUICK: task description - COMPLETE'
Includes brief summary of what was done
If progress.md doesn't exist, skips logging (non-FADE project)

userStories.title: Quick mode boundaries
userStories.description: As a developer, I want quick mode to have sensible boundaries so it doesn't become a loophole for skipping planning
acceptanceCriteria: Quick mode prompt limits scope to single-file or few-file changes
If task seems large, Claude should suggest creating a PRD instead
Quick mode does not run in loop (single execution)
No regression test generation for quick tasks

userStories.title: Quick mode with YOLO
userStories.description: As a developer, I want 'fade quick --yolo' to run without permission prompts for maximum speed
acceptanceCriteria: fade quick --yolo passes --dangerously-skip-permissions to Claude
fade quick (without --yolo) uses normal permission model
Behavior matches fade run --yolo pattern

technicalNotes.promptTemplate: Minimal prompt: read FADE.md (if exists), do the task, commit with conventional format, log to progress.md (if exists), done.
technicalNotes.noLoop: Quick mode is single-shot. No STORY_DONE/ALL_COMPLETE signals. Claude just does the task and exits.
technicalNotes.gsdComparison: GSD's /gsd:quick has similar purpose. FADE's version is simpler - no phase tracking, just task + commit + log.
